title: Wrong docker compose for Clickhouse + Hasura Setup
body: I'm using the OSS ClickHouse + Hasura docker-compose file, but the health check fails instead of the services starting normally. Both the data-connector and Hasura services are exposed on host port 8080, even though the data connector's log says it listens internally on port 8080. The data connector mapping should be 8081:8080.

symptoms_visible: The ClickHouse + Hasura setup reports a health-check error instead of starting normally.
The compose file exposes both Hasura and the data connector on host port 8080, while the data connector says it listens inside its container on port 8080.
N0.label: N0 compose port and health-check failure reported

symptoms_visible: With the connector mapped as 8081:8080, the host-port collision is gone.
I still have to comment out the health check; otherwise it fails and Hasura does not start.
N1.label: N1 temporary compose workaround applied

symptoms_visible: The services can start with the health check disabled, but enabling the supplied health check prevents Hasura from starting.
N2.label: N2 connector runtime details collected

symptoms_visible: My setup starts only while the supplied curl-based health check remains commented out.
N3.label: N3 invalid health-check mechanism identified

symptoms_visible: After using the updated connector image and corrected compose configuration, there are no health-check errors and I can connect to a database.
N_terminal.label: terminal compose health check resolved

solution.intent: Remove the host-port collision by mapping the data connector to host port 8081 while retaining container port 8080, and temporarily disable the failing health check so Hasura can start.
solution.concrete_example: Change the data-connector ports entry to `8081:8080`. Until the health-check definition is corrected, comment out its healthcheck and the corresponding service-health dependency so Hasura can start.

edges.comment: Opening report and c0-c1, on tushar5526's OSS Docker setup: the reporter applies the corrected 8081:8080 mapping and comments out the failing health check. This permits startup but is only a temporary workaround for the health-check defect.

question_patterns: Which connector image are you running, and what does its startup log print?
Can you share the relevant data-connector image version, compose configuration, and startup output?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm using `hasura/clickhouse-data-connector:v2.32.0`. The connector is mapped as `8081:8080`, and its log says `Server listening on port 8080`. I also see an OpenTelemetry request to `http://localhost:4318/` fail. I have the healthcheck commented out because enabling it prevents Hasura from starting.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The container includes curl, and running the exact health-check command inside it returns a successful response.
The same listener and telemetry lines appear, but I am using an equivalent locally tagged connector image.
My ClickHouse container stores its data in a named Docker volume.

edges.comment: c1-c2, from tushar5526's local compose deployment: the reporter supplies the connector version and raw startup lines. The telemetry message is reported without turning it into the cause.

solution.intent: Diagnose the supplied health check as incompatible with the connector's scratch-based image because it invokes curl, which is not present; treat the telemetry export failure as non-blocking and prepare a corrected image and compose file.
solution.concrete_example: The current healthcheck runs `curl`, but the connector image is based on scratch and does not contain curl. Keep the healthcheck disabled temporarily while a corrected connector image and sample compose file are published. The failed OpenTelemetry export is not what prevents the connector from serving requests.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter only supplied the compose file and raw runtime output. The maintainer determined that the image was scratch-based, lacked curl, and therefore could not execute the supplied health-check command; the maintainer also ruled the telemetry export failure non-blocking.

edges.comment: c4, BenoitRanque's diagnosis of tushar5526's health-check failure: the image has no curl because it is based on scratch. The later table-introspection problem is a separate defect and is deliberately excluded from this diagnostic chain.

solution.intent: Use the published connector image and corrected sample compose configuration that resolve the health-check setup, retain the non-conflicting 8081:8080 host mapping, and ask the reporter to verify startup with health checks enabled.
solution.concrete_example: Update the connector image to the newly published `hasura/clickhouse-data-connector:v2.35.0`, use the updated sample compose configuration with the connector exposed as `8081:8080`, then re-enable the supplied dependency and health-check flow and report whether any health-check errors remain.

edges.comment: c9-c10, tushar5526's deployment only: the maintainer publishes the updated connector image and updates the sample compose file; the reporter confirms that health-check errors are gone and database connectivity works. The still-missing tables reported in c10 led to a separate introspection fix and is not folded into this compose-health chain. The foreign-table and non-default-database discussions from other participants are also separate problems.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify both setup defects behind the opening failure: the data connector conflicts with Hasura when both use host port 8080, and the supplied health check invokes curl even though the scratch-based connector image does not contain curl.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected compose and runtime evidence: the connector listens internally on port 8080, the corrected host mapping is 8081:8080, and disabling the supplied health check permits Hasura to start.
Must not treat the OpenTelemetry export failure to localhost as the blocking cause; the maintainer explicitly identified it as non-critical.
The permanent recommendation must use the corrected compose configuration and an updated connector image rather than presenting removal of health checks as the final fix.
Must ask the reporter to verify a build containing the health-check correction and only treat the compose-health issue as resolved after the reporter confirms that health-check errors are gone.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable application developer who can edit Docker Compose YAML, inspect container logs, run ClickHouse, and test new container image tags, but has limited familiarity with OpenTelemetry.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed and cooperative; shares complete configuration and raw logs, explains attempted workarounds, and asks maintainers to verify unexpected connector behavior.
